page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Within it, a diagram of the passive conjugation sits between the first paragraph and the German paragraph. Headings are centred. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left.

main_text.p: Cicero inquit, Epistol.221. Quos spero brevitem-pore societate victoriæ tecum copulatos fore.

p.bl: Cicero sagt / welche ich hoffe daß sie in kurtzer zeit durch gesellschafft der uberwindung mit dir werden vereiniget werden.

main_text.head: Gerundia.
main_text.p: Amando, wen er/ die/ das geliebet wird. Docen-do, wen gelehret wird. Legendo, wen gelesen wird. Audiendo, wen gehöret wird. Ferendo, wen getra-gen wird.
main_text.head: Supina.
main_text.p: Donatus passivorum Gerundia & Supina omisit, cum tamen apud Authores occurrant: ut, Alitur vi-tium, vivitq; tegendo, Virgilius, id est ut exponit Do-minus Philippus Melanchthon, dum tegitur. Digna res auditu, hoc est, ut audiatur.
Passivam imitantur formam, & significationem habent activam: ut, prælior, ich streite/nicht ich wer-de gestritten / præliaris vel præliare, præliatur, præ-liamur, præliamini, præliantur.
Prælier, prælieris vel prælierē, prælietur, prælie-mur, præliemini, præliéntur.

page.notes: Small circle-like marks stand beside the line "Digna res auditu" and at the left of "Wir/ihr/die"; they look like ornaments or stray marks and are not transcribed. The word "præliéntur" is read with an accent that is uncertain. The German text is set in black letter and is marked <bl>. Long s is rendered as s. "vberwindung" is printed with v for the vowel u and is given as "uberwindung".
